support: Najitra Didi, from Lakhimpur district, Assam, represents the Hariyani Mising Gaon Mohila Self-Help Group, which she helped form with ten women in 2011. She has trained women in weaving since 1984. At the SARAS Aajeevika Mela 2026 in Gurugram, her stall's handwoven Muga silk sarees - priced between Rs 30,000 and Rs 70,000 - crossed Rs 3 lakh in sales within the first few days alone, as buyers increasingly sought handloom over machine-made goods. Four decades of teaching a craft, and a market finally catching up to its value.
